title: Reveal words, not strokes
statement: When text or a model answer appears bit by bit, reveal it in whole words or chunks in step with the explanation, not by slow letter-by-letter tracing.
example: In one study, whole-word appearance beat letter tracing on recall with d=.97.
detail: A research-boundary review checked two studies an outside review cited (`grade3-reading/artifacts/feedback-devfactory-2026-09-10/analysis-current-courses/RESEARCH-BOUNDARIES.md`, section 1). In a paper comparing fonts and reveal styles in narrated videos, Study 1, with 12 university adults and pseudowords, found whole-word appearance beat tracing on recall, d=.97 (Ram & Zhao 2022); a study of diagrams drawn during narration, four experiments with 484 college students, found conditional transfer benefits, not a universal effect (Fiorella & Mayer 2016, https://doi.org/10.1037/edu0000065). The review concludes that progressive modelling with synchronized explanation is plausible, that slow letter tracing that obstructs reading should be avoided, and that a chunked reveal is a reasonable prototype.
against: Both studies used adults and non-reading tasks; with typeface held constant, whole-word against tracing was d=.74 with corrected p=.077/.076, a trend rather than a significant contrast; and the paper compares no single-word reveal against chunks and sets no child-specific speed (the same file, lines 17-21).
